No SA: Sexual Assault requires non-consensual sexual contact or threat of contact. The customer was passed out, making contact impossible and his actions involuntary.

No Indecent Exposure: This crime requires the act to be willful (intentional) and have a lewd purpose (sexual gratification or offense). A person who is passed out cannot form that intent.

Pleading not guilty at arraignment is required under law for all felonies in NY state. It is not a statement of guilt or innocence, it is simply a procedural requirement. If she had tried to plead guilty, it would have been deemed a nullity and a not guilty plea would have been entered on her behalf.

An arraignment is simply the commencement of proceedings. The prosecutor is then required to provide the defendant with the evidence against them (discovery) as well as any exculpatory “Brady” material in their possession. No plea can be entered until the prosecutor has certified discovery compliance and the defense has had a chance to examine and investigate the evidence and potential defenses.

The plea that is entered is “not guilty” because under the law, unless and until the prosecutor has proven guilt beyond a reasonable doubt….that person is legally presumed “not guilty”. It is factually an accurate plea, but does not necessarily mean it is the final plea position.

If she had tried to plead guilty, it would have been deemed a nullity and a not guilty plea would have been entered on her behalf.

An arraignment is simply the commencement of proceedings. The prosecutor is then required to provide the defendant with the evidence against them (discovery) as well as any exculpatory “Brady” material in their possession. No plea can be entered until the prosecutor has certified discovery compliance and the defense has had a chance to examine and investigate the evidence and potential defenses.

The plea that is entered at that point is “not guilty” because under the law, unless and until the prosecutor has proven guilt beyond a reasonable doubt….that person is legally presumed “not guilty”. It is factually an accurate plea, but does not necessarily mean it is the final plea position.

@JohnRunyon Fun things about easements. And even the sidewalks a municipality may put on them.
- They exist to allow widening of a road without dealing with Eminent Domain claims on every plot.
- Easement are "your" yard when it comes to mowing, removing snow and ice, raking leaves, and keeping it clear of debris. They'll happily fine you for failing that. They will also tax you for the square footage.
- Easements are the municipalities' property when it comes time to widen a road, dig to bury or repair utilities, or make other public improvements.
- If there is an injury or other claim for an incident that happened on that easement, the municipality will work hard to make sure it is YOUR insurance, and not theirs, that pays the claims.
- If the sidewalk begins to crumble, lift, or otherwise break, even if such damage leads to injury, they'll put it on a "we'll get around to it" list. While you still might face insurance claims from injured people.

A delivery person's implied consent to be on private property is limited to the act of delivery itself. Once that purpose is completed, or if they deviate significantly from that purpose (e.g., by lingering, opening doors, or filming inside the home), their presence becomes unauthorized. Penal Law § 140.05 (simple trespass) and Penal Law § 140.10 (Criminal trespass in the third degree).

Under New York law, posting non-consensual nude videos or photos is a criminal and civil offense Penal Code § 245.15 and Civil Rights Law 52-B.

New York Penal Law § 250.45 defines Unlawful Surveillance in the Second Degree. Recording someone through a open door or window without their consent while they are in a place where they have a reasonable expectation of privacy, for the purpose of amusement, profit, or sexual gratification, falls under this law. Let me try to clear up the “not guilty” plea and why it has no bearing on the case at this stage. The plea of not guilty is symbolic. In New York, the local criminal courts only have preliminary jurisdiction over felony offenses. A defendant charged with a felony cannot enter a plea in the local criminal courts - the court lacks trial jurisdiction over the felony. Thus the felony proceeding can only be initiated in local criminal court.
In order for a plea to be entered, she will either be 1. Indicted by a grand jury and arraigned in the County Court; 2. Enter a plea of guilty to a negotiated plea in County Court as part of a Superior Court Information; 3. The DA Office moves the local criminal court to reduce the felony to a misdemeanor at which time she would need to be arraigned on the misdemeanor in local criminal court which would retain jurisdiction.
